content.title: About
content.content: Pancakes are thin, round cakes made from a liquid batter cooked on a skillet. Traditionally they are prepared with wheat flour, eggs, milk, and a small amount of sugar. Pancakes can be served sweet with toppings such as jam, honey, cottage cheese, or fruit, as well as savory with meat, fish, or vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pancakes are known worldwide: in Russia they are called “bliny”, in France “crêpes”, and in Japan “okonomiyaki” (in a thicker form).
The tradition of eating pancakes on Maslenitsa is linked to bidding farewell to winter and welcoming spring.
The largest pancake ever made was prepared in Russia in 2015, measuring 15.6 m in diameter.
Pancakes are often used in culinary shows as a “canvas” for artistic dishes.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pancakes provide a quick source of energy thanks to the carbohydrates they contain.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk in the batter supply a modest amount of complete protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour and milk deliver B1, B2, and niacin, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Milk contributes to bone and tooth health by providing calcium and phosphorus.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: The thin texture of pancakes makes them easy to digest, suitable for light diets.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑flour pancakes can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Pancakes may cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Fat content from frying
items.content: Cooking in oil adds fat; using a low‑smoke‑point oil or minimal oil can reduce this.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pancakes hot, rolled or folded. They can be brushed with butter, dusted with powdered sugar, drizzled with honey, or paired with berries, cottage cheese, caviar, ham, or vegetable fillings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool pancakes are placed in an airtight container and kept in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in bags, separating layers with parchment paper; reheat on a skillet after thawing.
